record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.original_question: Do there exist, in ZFC, countably compact topological groups G and H such that the product G × H is not countably compact?

evidence.quote:
Problem 11. Construct in ZF C countably compact topological groups G and H
such that their product G × H is not countably compact.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is called countably compact if every countable open cover of $X$ has a finite subcover, equivalently, if every infinite subset of $X$ has an accumulation point in $X$. A topological group is a group $G$ endowed with a topology (here assumed Hausdorff) such that the multiplication map $G \times G \to G$ and the inversion map $G \to G$ are continuous. The product $G \times H$ of two topological groups is the cartesian product with the product topology and componentwise group operation.

Working only within the standard Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with the Axiom of Choice (ZFC), without assuming any additional set-theoretic hypotheses such as the Continuum Hypothesis or Martin's Axiom, decide whether there exist countably compact topological groups $G$ and $H$ such that the product topological group $G \times H$ fails to be countably compact, and, if so, construct such a pair.
artifact.status_search_result: Hrušák, van Mill, Ramos-García, and Shelah constructed in ZFC a countably compact Boolean group without non-trivial convergent sequences, answering a 1980 question of van Douwen. Combining this with a theorem of van Douwen, they obtained in ZFC two countably compact topological groups whose product is not countably compact, solving the question. The result appeared around 2021.

status_evidence.title: Countably compact groups without non-trivial convergent sequences (Hrušák, van Mill, Ramos-García, Shelah)
status_evidence.snippet: Construction in ZFC of a countably compact group without non-trivial convergent sequences; using van Douwen's theorem, this answers in ZFC Comfort's question on non-productivity of countable compactness for topological groups.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is solved in ZFC: there exist countably compact topological groups whose product is not countably compact.

status_evidence.title: A van Douwen-like ZFC theorem for small powers of countably compact groups without non-trivial convergent sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Builds on the ZFC construction of countably compact groups without non-trivial convergent sequences and the resolution of Comfort's productivity question.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the ZFC resolution of the productivity of countable compactness for topological groups.
